stemMd: Which statement cannot be true in any permitted order?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Work and Letters must occupy consecutive positions, in either order.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Work and Letters must not occupy consecutive positions.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Memory must not be in position 2.

explanationMd:
Test whether each proposed statement can be added consistently to the rules. "Memory must not be in position 2." is incompatible with every permitted order. The alternative statements each have a complete valid example, given in their feedback. To check impossibility, enumerate placements for the most restricted item or block, then remove every case breaking a rule.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Cities → Memory → Customs → Work → Letters
- Cities → Memory → Letters → Work → Customs
- Customs → Memory → Letters → Cities → Work
- Letters → Memory → Customs → Cities → Work

Rules Memory must be in position 2. Cities must precede Work. Exactly 1 other item must occur between Customs and Letters. leave 4 valid orders: Cities>Memory>Customs>Work>Letters; Cities>Memory>Letters>Work>Customs; Customs>Memory>Letters>Cities>Work; Letters>Memory>Customs>Cities>Work. Choice true counts: a=2, b=0, c=1, d=2; impossible requires zero matches.
